overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals that first-person high-stakes 'What If You Fell Into...' cosmic hazard concepts and extreme planetary survival scenarios drive peak retention and engagement (800-1,050+ views, up to 3.7% like ratio). Conversely, over-recycled neuroscience trivia ('fake memories', 'songs stuck in head') and repeated re-uploads completely flatline below 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person 'What If You Fell Into / Visited' Extreme Cosmic Environments
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles using visceral what-if immersion like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) dramatically outperform third-person trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Frame cosmic and extreme science phenomena through direct second-person sensory survival scenarios ('What If You...').

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Planetary Physics & Extreme Contrast Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views, 25 likes) consistently beat standard animal or biology facts.
winning_patterns.action: Pair a paradoxical material or extreme physical state (e.g., solid liquid metal, diamond oceans, light-absorbing atmospheres) with high-contrast visual pacing.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' was published 4 times across different days and consistently flopped with 5, 10, and 53 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' gained only 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic text-heavy brain psychology facts unless tied to a high-stakes visual survival or mystery micro-story.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple uploads of identical topics ('Why Space Is Completely Silent', 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts') saw severe decay upon repeated posting.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict deduplication in production pipelines; never reuse published topics without a completely distinct angle or fresh narrative.

next_video.opening_direction: Instant POV descent toward a glowing, pulsing magnetar with the hook: 'If you stepped within 600 miles of this dead star, you wouldn't burn—your atomic structure would literally be erased.'

next_video.reason: Aligns directly with top-tier channel performers (21-second exoplanet/extreme space survival what-ifs) while introducing a totally unaddressed, highly cinematic cosmic entity.
